assertions.name: quadrature_converged
assertions.source: N=96 vs N=128 at a/b = phi agree to 2.792e-15 relative. Set at 1e-12 because the 10*pi^2 comparison below turns on a discrepancy of 5.9e-5, and that verdict is only meaningful if the quadrature error is orders below it.

assertions.name: golden_ratio_value_is_NOT_exactly_ten_pi_squared
assertions.source: E_total(phi) = 98.70181967865272 against 10*pi^2 = 98.69604401089359: ratio 1.00005851975, a discrepancy of 5.852e-5. The quadrature is converged to 2.792e-15, TEN ORDERS below that, so this is a genuine near-miss and not numerical error. At N=64 and four decimals it reads as 1.0000, which is how it would have been written down as an identity.

assertions.name: golden_ratio_is_not_the_family_minimum
assertions.source: The family minimum over a/b in [1.5, 2.1] is 97.583276794341 at a/b = 1.817, which is 1.133% BELOW the golden-ratio value. Same shape as the Hopf calibration, where the standard picture sat 7.3% above the minimum.

assertions.name: equal_circles_are_degenerate
assertions.source: At a = b the three orthogonal circles TOUCH: min separation squared = 1.66614e-143. Measured, not assumed -- it is why the family needs a != b at all.

assertions.name: TOPOLOGY_NOT_VERIFIED_across_the_scan
assertions.source: DELIBERATE ZERO, recording a known gap rather than a result. Nothing here checks that the configuration stays BORROMEAN as a/b varies -- only that the components do not touch. The Hopf calibration's assertion 4 records the identical trap: a scan guarded only against touching walked into a SPLIT link and 'minimised' below a proved bound. Two reasons this is less likely here -- the energy RISES on both sides of the interior minimum (142.6 at a/b=1.1, 149.5 at 6.0), rather than running away; and pairwise linking number is 0 by construction for the Borromean carrier, so there is no linking-number guard to write. But less likely is not verified. The family minimum above must NOT be cited as the Borromean energy minimum until the topology is checked.

description: Borromean cross energy over the classical three-orthogonal-ellipse family, using the integrator calibrated against the proved E(Hopf) = 2*pi^2. Bean qou-o6ml route (2). Reports the golden-ratio value, its convergence, and the family minimum -- and REFUTES the tempting reading that the golden-ratio value is exactly 10*pi^2.

family_minimum.caveat: TOPOLOGY NOT VERIFIED across the scan -- see the assertion of the same name. This is NOT claimed to be the Borromean energy minimum.

data.pair_convention: E_total sums UNORDERED pairs, the convention in which Agol-Marques-Neves state E(Hopf) >= 2*pi^2 and in which the calibration reproduces it. Doubling gives the ordered-pair value.
